items.title: 'Russia's invasion of Ukraine could have warned Trump from the pitfalls he now faces in Iran'
items.description: Like Vladimir Putin in Ukraine, Trump underestimated the Iranian regime when he went to war with it. According to Le Monde's Gilles Paris, those failures could serve as a warning to Xi Jinping about how to bring Taiwan back under China's control.

items.title: Putin hails Russia's test launch of a new ballistic missile
items.description: Russia test-fired a new intercontinental ballistic missile as part of efforts to modernize its nuclear forces. The nuclear-armed Sarmat missile would enter combat service at the end of the year.

items.title: Ceasefire in sight? What's next for Russia's war in Ukraine
items.description: Four years since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, is the end finally in sight? DW spoke to US political experts about why they think US home elections could bring about a ceasefire.

items.title: Using No Soldiers, Just Robots - How Ukraine Captured A Russian Position
items.description: Robots and drones were used by Ukrainian forces to capture a Russian position without an infantry assault in what Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a historic first in the war. Speaking to Current Time, troops involved in the operation are now revealing details.

items.title: TV Rain Editor-in-Chief Jailed 8 Years in Absentia Over War ‘Fakes’
items.description: Tikhon Dzyadko, who serves as editor-in-chief at TV Rain, was accused of spreading false information about the Russian armed forces.

items.title: As Russia pushes spring offensive, shift on battlefield buoys Ukrainians
items.description: Russia is no longer making major battlefield gains. If anything, it’s been Ukraine, aided by its technological prowess, taking back small pieces of territory. After a punishing winter, Ukraine is in a surprisingly encouraging place.

items.title: Armed drones leading cause of civilian death in Sudan war: UN rights chief
items.description: Drones caused more than 80 per cent of civilian deaths in Sudan’s war during the first four months of 2026, killing at least 880 people, the UN human rights chief said on Monday, warning that escalating drone warfare could push the conflict into an even deadlier phase.
